Stevenson played for six teams in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) during a 13-year career. He originally committed to play at the [[University of Kansas]], but decided to enter the NBA directly from high school and was picked by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 23rd selection of the [[2000 NBA draft]]. He was a member of the [[Dallas Mavericks]] team that won an NBA championship in 2011. In 2017, Stevenson joined [[Power (basketball)|Power]], one of the eight [[BIG3]] basketball league teams. ==Early life== Stevenson was born in [[Fresno, California]]. His father, Darryl Stevenson, never married his mother Genice Popps, and eventually was forcibly placed in a facility after threatening family members and diagnosed as schizophrenic. Darryl signed a court order agreeing he had a duty to support his son, but eventually murdered his own mother Clara by strangling her; he died of cancer at the age of 36 in prison. DeShawn's name was tattooed on his chest.http://twp.com/BETTER/detail.jsp?key=343211&rc=to&p=1&all=1 {{dead link|date=January 2012}}{{cite news|title=Stevenson follows dad's dream to NBA|url=http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2000/jul/22/stevenson_follows_dads/|work=Lawrence Journal-World|agency=Associated Press|date=July 22, 2000|access-date=2008-11-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081002165223/http://www2.ljworld.com/news/2000/jul/22/stevenson_follows_dads/|archive-date=2008-10-02|url-status=dead}} Due to the absence of his father, DeShawn lived with his [[godparent]]s in [[Easton, California|Easton]], [[California]]. He played high school ball at the same school where his father had played, and won a state championship his junior year. Stevenson signed with the [[Kansas Jayhawks]] in the fall of his senior year. Jayhawks head coach [[Roy Williams (coach)|Roy Williams]] called him his "most gifted recruit ever".{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ku-recruit-going-pro-after-all/|title=KU Recruit Going Pro After All|website=[[CBS News]]}} As a senior, Stevenson averaged 30.4 points, 9.7 rebounds and 6.2 assists a game. He was named to the [[McDonald's All-American]] team and scored 25 points to lead the West to a 146–120 win, and won the slam-dunk contest. Stevenson's mother advised him not to go straight to the NBA, but after there were irregularities with his [[SAT test]], because he claimed he didn't know any answers because his girlfriend allegedly did all his homework in high school, Stevenson did indeed enter the league straight out of high school.{{cite news|last=Bedore|first=Gary|title=Stevenson picks Kansas after all|url=http://newsnow.ljworld.com/cgi-bin/LiveIQue.acgi$rec=222311?jhawks|newspaper=Lawrence Journal-World|date=May 9, 2000|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010504023610/http://newsnow.ljworld.com/cgi-bin/LiveIQue.acgi%24rec%3D222311?jhawks|archive-date=May 4, 2001|url-status=dead}}{{cite news| url=http://www.oregonlive.com/sports/oregonian/john_canzano/index.ssf/2009/06/memphis_basketball_teaches_the.html | work=The Oregonian | title=Memphis basketball teaches the wrong lesson | date=June 5, 2009}} ==Professional career== === Utah Jazz (2000–2004) === Stevenson was picked by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 23rd selection of the [[2000 NBA draft]]. Stevenson appeared in 222 regular season games during his time with Utah. He averaged 5.9 ppg, 1.9 rpg, and 1.2 apg, in 16.7 mpg during that time. Stevenson played in five career playoff outings. At 19 years old, he became the youngest player to ever play and start for the Jazz during the 2000–01 season. In 2001, Stevenson finished second in the NBA [[Slam Dunk Contest]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/allstar2002/slamdunk/year_by_year.html |title=Slam Dunk Year-by-Year Results |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2007-12-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604011352/http://www.nba.com/allstar2002/slamdunk/year_by_year.html |archive-date=2011-06-04 |url-status=dead }} Later that year, Stevenson pleaded no contest to the offence of the criminal offence having sex with a minor, having sex with a 14-year-old girl.{{cite news| url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/2006-05-04-community-service_x.htm | work=USA Today | title=Athletes lightly punished after their day in court | first1=Michael | last1=McCarthy | first2=Jodi | last2=Upton | date=May 4, 2006 | access-date=May 1, 2010}} On March 16, 2003, Stevenson received widespread attention for shoving [[Ricky Davis]] of the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] after Davis deliberately missed a shot on his own basket in an attempt to record a [[triple-double]], when the Cavaliers were up 120–95.{{cite web|url=http://static.espn.go.com/nba/columns/aldridge_david/1525101.html|title=Davis should be punished for showing up Jazz|first=David|last=Aldridge|date=March 17, 2003|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 19, 2016}} On November 1, 2003, Stevenson scored a then-career-high 24 points in a loss against the Mavericks.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200311010DAL.html|title=Jazz vs Mavericks, November 1, 2003}} On February 19, 2004, Stevenson and a future second round draft pick were acquired by the [[Orlando Magic]] from the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for guard–forward [[Gordan Giricek]]. === Orlando Magic (2004–2006) === Stevenson played with the [[Orlando Magic]] for 2½ seasons. He had his best year during the 2005–06 season when he averaged 11.0 ppg, 2.9 rpg, and 2.0 apg. Stevenson opted out of the third and final year of his contract with Orlando, and on August 5, 2006, he signed a two-year minimum contract with the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2538921 |title=ESPN - Wizards sign former Magic guard Stevenson - NBA |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2006-08-05 |access-date=2012-01-23}} === Washington Wizards (2006–2010) === [[File:LebronStevenson.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Stevenson and [[LeBron James]] in April 2008. The two had a short feud after Stevenson called James "overrated".{{cite web|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|title=Stevenson: LeBron beef 'pretty much over'|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4678739/deshawn-stevenson-lebron-beef-pretty-much-over|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=December 22, 2021|date=May 28, 2011|archive-date=December 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222090316/https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4678739/deshawn-stevenson-lebron-beef-pretty-much-over|url-status=live}}]] On August 5, 2006, Stevenson signed a two-year contract with the Washington Wizards for the NBA minimum salary. Stevenson quickly adjusted to coach [[Eddie Jordan (basketball)|Eddie Jordan]]'s system, averaging 11.2 ppg, 2.7 rpg, and 2.7 apg in his first season with Washington. Following the 2006–07 season, he opted out of the second year of his contract to test free agency. On July 16, 2007, Stevenson re-signed with the Wizards on a four-year, $15 million deal.{{cite news| url=http://www.nba.com/news/429702.html?rss=true | work=NBA.com | title=NBA.com News Flash|date=July 16, 2007|access-date=March 17, 2014}} On the early morning of August 20, 2007, a 31-year-old man, Curtis Ruff, was shot and injured at Stevenson's home, following an argument with women who were invited from Destiny's Club in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]]. Circumstances of the incident remain unclear.{{cite web |url=http://www.wesh.com/news/13929862/detail.html |title=Man Injured In Shooting At NBA Player's Home |publisher=Wesh.com |date=2007-08-20 |access-date=2012-01-23 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229200745/http://www.wesh.com/news/13929862/detail.html |archive-date=2012-02-29 }} After Stevenson, with a sore knee, scored a career-high 33 points, including a game winning three-pointer as time expired in a February 25, 2008, victory over the [[New Orleans Hornets]], Wizards coach Eddie Jordan described Stevenson by saying, "He's a warrior, man, a true warrior. His confidence is growing, he's making threes, he's just a true pro. This is a man's league and he is man. In the dictionary next to that word there is a picture of DeShawn Stevenson."{{cite web |last=Magazine |first=Dime |url=http://dimemag.com/2008/02/worlds-apart/ |title=Worlds Apart | Dime Magazine (dimemag.com) : Daily NBA News, NBA Trades, NBA Rumors, Basketball Videos, Sneakers |publisher=dimemag.com |date=2008-02-26 |access-date=2012-01-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120304131319/http://dimemag.com/2008/02/worlds-apart/ |archive-date=2012-03-04 |url-status=dead }} At the start of the [[2008–09 NBA season|2008–09 season]], Stevenson struggled and could not bring his offensive game to the level it had attained in 2007. As a result, Stevenson's minutes dipped slightly with the development of second year shooting guard [[Nick Young (basketball)|Nick Young]] and former Maryland standout [[Juan Dixon]]. === Dallas Mavericks (2010–2011) === [[File:DeShawn Stevenson at the Championship parade.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Stevenson at the [[Dallas Mavericks]] championship parade]] On February 13, 2010, Stevenson was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] along with [[Caron Butler]] and [[Brendan Haywood]] for [[Josh Howard]], [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]], [[James Singleton (basketball)|James Singleton]] and [[Quinton Ross]].{{cite web | title = MAVERICKS ACQUIRE BUTLER, HAYWOOD AND STEVENSON IN SEVEN-PLAYER TRADE | url = http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/mavericks_acquire_butler_hayward.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = 2010-02-13 | access-date = 2010-02-14}}{{cite web|first=Brad|last=Townsend|url=http://sportsday.dallasnews.com/dallas-mavericks/mavericksheadlines/2011/06/01/townsend-how-mavericksdeshawn-stevenson-went-from-troublemaker-to-perfectlife|title=Townsend: How Mavericks' DeShawn Stevenson went from troublemaker to 'perfect' life|work=DallasNews.com|publisher=[[Dallas News]]|date=June 1, 2011|access-date=December 20, 2016}} Stevenson became the first player in NBA history to wear number 92 on his jersey. Stevenson chose number 92 because he wore number 9 in Orlando and number 2 with Utah and Washington.{{cite web | title= NBA & ABA Players Who Wore Number 92 | url= https://www.basketball-reference.com/friv/numbers.cgi?number=92 | work = basketball-reference.com | date = 2010-03-15 | access-date = 2010-03-15}} He used his player option and made $4.15 million during the [[2010–11 NBA season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/nba/news/story?id=5214846 |title=Stevenson uses his Option |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=2010-05-24 |access-date=2012-01-23}} On June 12, 2011, the Mavericks won the [[NBA]] championship, defeating the [[LeBron James]]-led [[Miami Heat]] 105–95 in Game 6 of the [[2011 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]]. In that game, Stevenson made three of five three-point shots, scoring nine points.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2011/news/features/sekou_smith/06/13/mavs-game-6/index.html |title=Mavs' Big Team sheds negative labels with team's first title |work=NBA.com |date=2011-06-13 |access-date=2012-01-23 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160910044713/http://www.nba.com/2011/news/features/sekou_smith/06/13/mavs-game-6/index.html |archive-date=2016-09-10 }} === New Jersey Nets (2011–2012) === On December 23, 2011, Stevenson signed one-year $2.5 million contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets|New Jersey Nets]].{{cite web | title = NETS Sign DeShawn Stevenson | url = http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Stevenson_Signing_Release_111223.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = December 23, 2011 | access-date = December 23, 2011}} === Atlanta Hawks (2012–2013) === On July 11, 2012, the Nets traded Stevenson in a [[sign-and-trade]], along with [[Jordan Farmar]], [[Jordan Williams (basketball, born 1990)|Jordan Williams]], [[Anthony Morrow]], and [[Johan Petro]], to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for [[Joe Johnson (basketball)|Joe Johnson]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/2012_Offseason_Tracker.html#wallace | title=A Jolt of Joe for the Nets | publisher=Brooklyn Nets | date=July 11, 2012 | access-date=July 11, 2012 | author=Couch, Ben}} On August 2, 2013, he was waived by the Hawks.{{cite web |last=Links |first=Zachary |date=August 2, 2013 |title=Hawks Waive DeShawn Stevenson |url=http://www.hoopsrumors.com/2013/08/hawks-waive-deshawn-stevenson.html |access-date=August 2, 2013 |work=HoopsRumors.com}}{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=13953|title=Atlanta Hawks expected to add DeMarre Carroll|work=InsideHoops.com|date=August 2, 2013|access-date=August 2, 2013}} Stevenson played his final game on May 1, 2013, during Game 5 of the Eastern Conference's 1st Round. The Hawks lost the game 83 - 106 with Stevenson only playing 16 seconds. Stevenson formally announced his retirement three and half years later on December 19, 2016.{{cite web|first=Tyler|last=Conway|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2682728-deshawn-stevenson-retires-latest-comments-and-reaction|title=DeShawn Stevenson Retires: Latest Comments and
